## Characters

### Alex Phantum

**Role:** Seventeen-year-old Keel worker, mechanically capable pump and machinery repairer, Adrian Phantum’s son, and the inheritor of Adrian’s debt, workshop, devices, and disputed intellectual estate. His parental household liability transfers to him at seventeen. The transfer display records a debt balance of **418,607 credits**, earnings of **40 credits that day**, projected clearance in **28.7 years**, and restricted travel. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 2, 5; rules/ancestry.md)`

**Look:** Lean, mechanically capable, and visibly mixed Indigenous Andean and European-descended. He should resemble Adrian through jaw, eyes or eye shape, expressions, head tilt, posture, and habitual gestures, while also carrying substantial visible inheritance from his unrevealed Indigenous Andean mother. His appearance must quietly raise the question of who he inherited the rest of himself from. `(rules/ancestry.md)`

He wears worn mining clothes and carries a weathered tool bag. His clothes and body can be dirty from work; his guarded posture reads as self-reliant rather than defeated. He has scarred, work-rough hands and a wrist guard bearing a carved balanced water-drop mark. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 2, 6–8)`

Recurring objects include:
- a worn casino chip etched with a looping equation, found when he was six;
- a creased photograph of Adrian, often folded so Adrian’s face is partly hidden;
- Adrian’s altered paper map;
- a tool bag;
- later, the Measure and the Maker’s Seal. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 2, 10–14)`

**Voice:** Short, dry, concrete, skeptical, mechanical, and mildly abrasive when defensive. He trusts vibration, pressure, wear, physical evidence, and what people actually do more than labels or official descriptions. He uses Keel vocabulary such as **clean, hot, burned, crooked, thin, solid, patched, ghost, paper-clean, fitch,** and **salvo**. `(rules/vocabulary.md)`

Useful established lines include:
- “Then don't approve it. Just notice it works.”
- “I've also got his debt.”
- “Everything has a price, Ada.”
- “Who decided they get our water?” `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 2–4; rules/vocabulary.md)`

He can be funny, but humor is usually a defensive reduction of the immediate problem:
- “Okay. That's... new.”
- “So I inherited his lab fees.”
- “Staying I can predict. Twenty-eight point seven years.”
- “This is the only way out that isn't a sentence.” `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 5)`

He does not naturally speak in political, academic, activist, bureaucratic, or socially conscious abstractions. When he reaches a larger idea, he reduces it to physical evidence or a choice:
- “Truth doesn't need authorization.”
- “I know what I traded.”
- “I didn't fix any of it. I just made sure nobody can keep it hidden.” `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 12–13; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, p. 8)`

**Who they are:** Alex begins as a young worker whose immediate objective is escape from Keel, debt, and a future he believes has already been assigned. He is skeptical of official records because he repeatedly sees machinery and measurements contradict them. He is self-reliant, observant, brave under physical pressure, and instinctively inclined to repair what is in front of him.

He is not naturally a public leader or theorist. His understanding develops through concrete choices:
- who owns something;
- who gets paid;
- who carries the risk;
- what a record says versus what a pipe does;
- what he gives up when he chooses one path over another. `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 10–12)`

His central contradiction is that he wants personal freedom and an exit from Keel, but he repeatedly chooses responsibility to other people when the choice becomes real. He is tempted by debt clearance, legal status, private escape, and concentrated authority. He is also tempted by the fantasy that he could fix everything himself if given enough power. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5, 11–14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 3–8)`

**Relationships:**
- **Adrian Phantum:** Alex’s absent father. Alex was two when Adrian disappeared from his life and remembers nothing directly. He has inherited contradictory accounts: a gambler and debtor, a worker, an inventor, and a man who built safeguards and bet on Alex. Alex begins by treating Adrian’s legacy as debt and suspicion. He gradually accepts that Adrian can have been both a father who left and a person who gave everything to a consequential wager. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–11; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 7–9)`
- **Alex’s mother:** She left Adrian after he lost everything. Nothing else about her is learned. Alex’s appearance carries her unrevealed Indigenous Andean inheritance, but the story must not supply her biography. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md; rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Grandmother Phantum:** Alex’s caregiver and the keeper of Adrian’s workshop entrance. She sometimes mistakes Alex for Adrian, but she also preserves Adrian’s objects and gives Alex the access he needs. Alex is gentle and patient with her, even when her memory hurts him. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 4–10)`
- **Ada Veyra:** His closest companion and emotional counterweight. They grew up in Keel and share local speech, but Ada is more attentive to obligations, fear, avoidance, and what people refuse to say. Alex looks upward toward personal escape; Ada looks downward toward the people who stayed. Their intimacy is established through humor, silence, physical proximity, and disagreement rather than declarations. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–5; rules/vocabulary.md)`
- **Bi11bot:** Mentor, inherited companion, investigator, and moral friction. Alex is initially startled by him and skeptical of his claims, but increasingly trusts his questions without surrendering his own judgment. Bi11bot repeatedly refuses to choose for him. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–5, 11–12)`
- **Tomas:** An older miner who knew Adrian and recognizes Alex through his behavior. Tomas helps him because Alex stops to save a stranger. Their relationship is grounded in work, risk, and mutual practical action rather than sentiment. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`
- **Mera Vale:** Institutional opponent and later witness to the damage caused by concentrated authority. Alex challenges her without adopting her polished vocabulary. He eventually thanks her for telling him the parts that make her look bad, but does not absolve her. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 3, 10–11; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 3–10)`
- **Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr, and Ren Okafor:** Collaborators whose work Alex helps reconnect. His instinct is to solve the technical problem physically, but his more important change is recognizing that the work is not his alone to transfer or own. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4–15)`
- **Leona Veyra:** Ada’s mother. Alex deliberately stays outside their first reunion, recognizing that this is not his scene to enter. Later he participates when the question becomes collective responsibility. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2–5, 11–13)`

**Habits and tells:** He tests mechanisms with his palm and head tilted, feeling vibration rather than trusting the gauge. He turns the casino chip in his pocket without noticing. He crosses his arms in an armored stance when uncertain or defensive. He notices what does not belong: clean bolts in a dead mine, condensation, a wet pipe, an improvised bracket that works. He tends to reach for physical action before abstract explanation. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 2–3; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–12)`

Under pressure, he first tries to make himself forgettable, then violates that plan when someone is in danger. He crosses the assigned-zone line and accepts a **40-credit wage forfeiture** to help Tomas. Later he gives up a private mapped escape route to send Keel the evidence of the water diversion. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5–8, 11–13)`

**History:** Alex was two when Adrian disappeared. Adrian’s absence was explained to him through family stories, including the claim that Adrian gambled and left. Alex found the etched casino chip at six. He grew up in Keel with his grandmother and became a worker capable of repairing old infrastructure with salvaged parts. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–5, 8–10; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 2)`

**In existing drafts:** Alex repairs an unapproved pump bracket; refuses to sign away Adrian’s estate despite the offer to erase his debt; uses the Measure to compare official water allocation with actual flow; sends the discrepancy to Keel rather than preserving a private escape route; helps Tomas; rejects the idea that two people should rule everyone else; and invents a distributed decision structure rather than accepting executive authority for himself. These are draft actions and evidence of his developing character, not a binding script. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 2, 8–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5–14; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 10–15; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 3–8)`

**Arc:** Alex starts by wanting to leave Keel and escape a debt he sees as a sentence. Adrian’s workshop gives him a personal mystery, but the Measure forces him to choose between private escape and public truth. The Seal and Covenant then force him to distinguish making from owning, and authority from responsibility. By the end of the supplied material, he refuses concentrated power, accepts uncertainty, and chooses a structure in which decisions remain visible and distributed. He can leave, but staying beside Ada is now his choice rather than Keel’s sentence. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 2–5; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 11–14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 3–13)`

### Ada Veyra

**Role:** Alex’s longtime companion from Keel; practical organizer, observer of human motives, and participant in the search for Adrian’s safeguards. She later becomes Leona Veyra’s daughter in the course of the story. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–5; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 1–4)`

**Look:** Twenty years old, with long wind-tangled copper hair, freckles, and light teal-blue eyes. She wears a dark high-collared top, a rivet-studded strap across one shoulder, and a muted moss-green wrap at her neck. Her stance is steady and rooted. She is mixed Indigenous Andean and European/criolla; her lighter coloring can come from her other parent, while her facial structure, family resemblance, posture, and other features should visibly connect her to Leona. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 3; rules/ancestry.md)`

**Voice:** Ada shares Keel’s compressed, local vocabulary with Alex but is less mechanical and more interpersonal. She notices obligations, avoidance, fear, imbalance, hidden motives, and who is carrying a burden. She does not sound therapeutic or academically emotionally literate. `(rules/vocabulary.md)`

Characteristic vocabulary includes **clean, crooked, square, tied, loose, carrying, showing,** and **full cup**. Useful established lines include:
- “Not everything.”
- “He wouldn't just leave.”
- “That's not what you're mad about.”
- “You don't get to make that choice for them.”
- “Don't give me that much power.”
- “I just wanted it to be your choice.” `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–5; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 5, 12)`

She is comfortable letting silence sit. Her questions are often more consequential than Alex’s answers:
- “What if they were wrong?”
- “Who gave it that authority?”
- “Why didn't you come for me?”
- “Did you know where I was?” `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 4; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 2; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 5–6)`

**Who they are:** Ada is perceptive, steady, teasing when the pressure permits, and more concerned with obligations between people than with mechanisms alone. She does not want abstract power over Keel. She wants people affected by a decision to have a say in it and to be able to call a promise broken when it is broken. `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 9–11; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 5, 12)`

Her central concern is not merely whether a person is safe, but whether they were given a choice. She distinguishes protection from agency:
- “Safety isn't the same as agency.”
- “I don't want power over what happens to Keel. I want a say in it.” `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, p. 9; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, p. 12)`

She is also capable of practical risk. She marks Adrian’s plans from memory despite having no way to confirm them, organizes Keel’s aid network, and joins Alex because she wants to understand who decided Keel had to remain as it was—not because she has abandoned Keel. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5, 13–14)`

**Relationships:**
- **Alex:** Their bond is longstanding, intimate, teasing, and grounded in shared Keel experience. She challenges his escape instinct without trying to own his decision. She gives him coffee without creating a debt, shares information, follows him into danger, and refuses to let him turn shared responsibility into a two-person authority. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–5; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5, 14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 5, 12)`
- **Leona Veyra:** Ada believes Leona abandoned her, then learns Leona knew where she was and chose not to return. Ada refuses an easy apology or instant forgiveness. She asks Leona to show change publicly and gives permission to keep trying without declaring the relationship repaired. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2–5, 9–14)`
- **Mera Vale:** Mera protected Ada from a distance under a promise to Leona, but Ada identifies the gap between being watched and being known. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, p. 6)`
- **Bi11bot:** He treats her as a legitimate participant rather than merely Alex’s companion. She questions his explanations and keeps him from turning the safeguards into a purely technical problem. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–3; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 1–6)`

**Habits and tells:** She carries a riveted strap and often touches one of its rivets while thinking or withholding a reaction. She watches people’s hands, posture, and absences more than official displays. She lets silence remain instead of rescuing others from it. She organizes lists, bags, papers, and practical routes under pressure. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 3; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 2, 9; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 6)`

**History:** Ada grew up in Keel and believed her mother, Leona, had disappeared or died. She was separated from Leona during the Water Wars at age five. Leona knew within a year where she was but did not return, believing distance kept her safe. Ada spent fifteen years carrying the unresolved question of whether she had been abandoned or orphaned. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2–9)`

**In existing drafts:** Ada brings Alex a birthday drink and explicitly tells him he owes nobody for it; challenges his assumptions about Adrian; joins the Site 6 escape; notices the discrepancy between official water records and actual delivery; organizes supplies and people after the water evidence reaches Keel; identifies Leona’s failure as a failure of agency; and rejects executive authority when Alex offers to share it with her. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–5; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5–14; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 5–14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 1–12)`

**Arc:** Ada begins as someone who believes people in Keel have stopped trying and who quietly carries an unanswered family wound. She becomes the person most able to name the human cost hidden inside technical or institutional solutions. Her reunion with Leona does not resolve the wound; instead, Ada demands visible accountability. By the end of the supplied material, she chooses neither concentrated authority nor forced sacrifice. She remains with Alex because she wants their choices—and her own—to be choices. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 3; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 5–14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 5, 12)`

### Bi11bot

**Role:** A small inherited repair and advice robot built by Adrian. He is Alex’s companion, guide, witness, and question-asker. He carries Adrian’s recorded messages and knowledge of the safeguards but does not choose for Alex. `(rules/characters.md; drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–11)`

**Look:** Two expressive optical eyes; foldable enough to fit in a backpack; an old scarf. His eyes are wise, patient, and often quietly amused. He is never menacing. He should not be drawn with harsh or red eye light, predatory posture, looming angles, or his face swallowed by shadow. `(rules/characters.md)`

In the drafts he is a compact brass-and-ivory ceramic mechanical figure with a rotating lens ring, stiff mechanical arms, dust in his joints, and a shoulder-mounted projector. He can fold into Alex’s tool bag and pass as scrap. His chest contains fitted compartments for the Measure and a Covenant band. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 7–10; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5, 14; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, p. 12)`

**Voice:** Dry, economical, patient, precise, and warm underneath. He asks short questions rather than giving lectures. His voice combines Adrian’s workshop and engineering language with gambling, probability, financial literacy, and Bill Reynolds’s plain, failure-aware perspective. `(rules/stakeholders.md; rules/vocabulary.md)`

Recurring or useful lines include:
- “Thinking about it isn't doing it.”
- “Sealed isn't the same as gone.”
- “Good. Your father always said certainty was where mistakes began.”
- “Who carries the downside?”
- “Price isn't value.”
- “Valuable isn't the same as spendable.”
- “A debt is a tool. Tools become dangerous when you don't understand which end you're holding.”
- “The mechanism is sound. The premise is not.”
- “Noise isn't always error.”
- “Protective? A versatile word.”
- “Different failure mode.”
- “Still holding.” `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 9–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 7–12)`

His financial teaching follows **concrete example → question → concept**, not definition → explanation → moral. He can ask:
- “Who owns it?”
- “Who gets paid?”
- “Who carries the risk?”
- “What happens if you're wrong?”
- “What are you giving up?”
- “Is that valuable, or merely expensive?” `(rules/vocabulary.md)`

**Who they are:** Bi11bot is observant, quietly funny, and protective without being controlling. He believes certainty creates mistakes, systems have tells, and every apparent upside must be examined alongside its downside. He knows that ownership, contribution, value, price, cost, debt, and control are not interchangeable.

He does not replace Alex’s judgment. He presents options, identifies costs, and leaves the choice with Alex:
- “Known: it's the only way in. Unknown: who's waiting. The choice is yours.”
- “Which is why I'm not choosing.”
- “Your father built three objects that each refuse to decide alone.” `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5, 11–12; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, p. 7)`

**Relationships:**
- **Adrian:** Adrian built Bi11bot and bet him that Alex would keep the chip. Bi11bot was present in Adrian’s workshop and carried the memory of Adrian’s final moments. He has spent fifteen years wondering whether Adrian was right about Alex. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–10; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 4–7)`
- **Alex:** He is Alex’s inherited companion but refuses to become Alex’s authority. He tests Alex with questions, carries the Measure, and waits until Alex has something worth doing before revealing more. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–5; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 11–13)`
- **Ada:** He recognizes her as someone whose judgment matters. He asks Alex whether she should stay before revealing the next stage of Adrian’s plan. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 1)`
- **TJ:** Bi11bot built TJ from spare parts to solve problems he could not solve himself. `(rules/characters.md)`

**Habits and tells:** His lens ring clicks when he focuses or turns his head. He often pauses before deciding how much not to say. He tilts his head politely. He asks one compact question rather than delivering a speech. He can fold into Alex’s tool bag and pretend to be scrap. In moments of emotional strain, his stillness becomes more pronounced rather than threatening. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–9; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5–7; rules/characters.md)`

**History:** Adrian built Bi11bot in the hidden workshop. Adrian’s final recording and final act were made in the old station while Alpha’s pursuit closed in. Bi11bot was not fully awake then and remembers only the last seconds clearly. He was later tasked with carrying Adrian’s map, messages, objects, and unresolved bet to Alex. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 6–10; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 4–7)`

**In existing drafts:** He introduces Alex to the workshop, carries the map, explains the safeguards, helps Alex use the Measure, protects the group from detection at Site 6, stores artifacts in his chest, relays Adrian’s message, and discloses that he has wondered for fifteen years whether Alex would fulfill Adrian’s bet. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–14; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 7–9)`

**Arc:** Bi11bot begins as the holder of answers and the custodian of Adrian’s plan. His meaningful change is not gaining authority but becoming more emotionally explicit: he admits that Adrian’s bet has been “on us” for fifteen years and acknowledges Alex’s own fourth choice as genuinely his. `(drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 7–9; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

### TJ

**Role:** Bi11bot’s companion and a small repair robot dog. TJ is the crossover character introduced early in Issue 01 at Site 6. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md)`

**Look:** Salvaged, mismatched parts visibly held together by magnets. His head, legs, body segments, and tail are separate pieces that snap together. He reads as a dog in every shape he takes. `(rules/characters.md)`

**Voice:** TJ does not talk. He communicates through body language, posture, and sounds. `(rules/characters.md)`

**Who they are:** Bi11bot built TJ from spare parts to solve problems Bi11bot could not solve himself. TJ can drop parts off, retrieve them, and rebuild himself into whatever shape a job needs. `(rules/characters.md)`

**Capabilities:** TJ can leave his head behind as a camera; drop his legs and send his slinky body segments through gaps; and reach into machinery, ducts, and walls to repair inaccessible components. `(rules/characters.md)`

**Relationships:** He is an extension of Bi11bot’s practical care and ingenuity, but not merely a tool. His dog behavior and nonverbal communication distinguish him from Bi11bot. `(rules/characters.md)`

**History:** He is assembled by Bi11bot from spare parts at Site 6. No further history is established. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md; rules/characters.md)`

**First consequential action:** At Site 6, Bi11bot assembles TJ from salvaged brackets, magnets, and cable fragments while Alex works. TJ’s head rolls away to watch the biometric gate before snapping back onto his body. When the hauling frame pins Tomas, TJ separates his legs and slinky body segments, enters the jammed mechanism, and releases the trapped support, giving Alex the opening to help Tomas and patch the ventilation line. He communicates only through movement and mechanical sounds. [FIXED for this revision] `(rules/decisions.md)`

**Arc:** No arc is established in the supplied material.

### Adrian Phantum

**Role:** Alex’s father; inventor, engineer, gambler by reputation and by practice, creator of Bi11bot, and builder of the three safeguards. His intellectual estate contains **312 patents**, including **47 restricted** and **19 disputed** records. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 2–4)`

**Look:** European-descended. He should visibly resemble Alex through jaw, eyes or eye shape, expressions, head tilt, posture, and habitual gestures, but Alex must not look like a younger duplicate of him. `(rules/ancestry.md)`

The clearest draft image shows Adrian in a hologram: a tired, steady-faced man whose expression can shift from a half-smile to seriousness. A worn photograph of him is repeatedly folded and unfolded by Alex. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 4, 10)`

**Voice:** His recorded voice is direct, warm, and deliberately incomplete. He tells Alex that answers must be earned:
- “You deserve answers. But they have to be earned.”
- “If I've done my job well... you'll become a better man than I ever was.”
- “Trust Bi11bot. But question everything... Especially me.” `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 10)`

His conceptual language combines probability, engineering, responsibility, and uncertainty. He is associated with the looping equation on Alex’s chip and with the line of thought that Alpha cannot choose to leap for a person. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 2–4)`

**Who they are:** Adrian is contradictory by design. Keel remembers him as a gambler and debtor, while his collaborators remember an inventor who built with other people and tried to prevent ownership from being separated from responsibility. He was willing to use gambling as a laboratory for probability and human behavior. His work is not presented as purely altruistic: he made bets, took risks, and left consequences for others to inherit.

**Relationships:**
- **Alex:** Adrian left Alex when Alex was two, but prepared a workshop, a map, Bi11bot, and a sequence of tests for him. He bet Bi11bot that Alex would keep the chip and designed the safeguards to answer to choices rather than possession. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 8–11; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–6)`
- **Alex’s mother:** She left Adrian after he lost everything. Nothing else is known or may be learned. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md)`
- **Grandmother Phantum:** She preserved Adrian’s workshop and objects and protected his secret from Alex until he was ready. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 5–6)`
- **Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr, and Ren Okafor:** He built water-related work with each of them, leaving each collaborator a separate piece or record outside the main system. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4–8)`
- **Leona Veyra and Mera Vale:** He built the Covenant with them during or after the Water Wars. He opposed granting Alpha emergency authority when Leona and Mera considered it. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 7–9)`

**Habits and tells:** He studies people’s faces and probability trees rather than merely cards. He uses physical objects—chips, keys, instruments, bands, workshop devices—to carry ideas. He leaves tests rather than explanations. His repeated visual inheritance in Alex is the head tilt, eyes, and posture. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 4)`

**History:** Adrian was involved in the creation of Alpha’s safeguards and later became the target of Alpha’s surveillance, financial restriction, public liability designation, and pursuit. Mera watched the sequence but could not override it. Adrian completed a final message and awakened Bi11bot in a flooded station before the bulkhead sealed. `(drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 3–6)`

**Present status:** Adrian died or was presumed dead when the monitoring station flooded and the bulkhead sealed. The story does not show a body, so his status remains an emotional absence and loss rather than a forensic certainty. [FIXED for this revision] `(rules/decisions.md)`

**In existing drafts:** He appears through photographs, recordings, memories, patent records, collaborator testimony, and the devices he leaves behind. Different characters’ accounts complicate rather than settle who he was. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 3–10; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 2–8; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 7–9)`

**Arc:** Adrian has no present-time arc. His posthumous function is to move from an absent, possibly selfish father in Alex’s inherited story to a contradictory person whose choices still require Alex’s judgment. His death is presumed from the flooded station, but the story does not turn his absence into a revealed reunion. `(rules/decisions.md)`

### Alex’s Mother

**Role:** Alex’s mother and Adrian’s former partner. Her identity is unrevealed.

**Look:** No canon look is established. Character design should assume that Alex inherited substantial visible Indigenous Andean ancestry from her, but the story must not identify her exact nation, community, appearance, or other biography. `(rules/ancestry.md)`

**Voice:** No voice is established.

**Who they are:** The only established fact is that she left Adrian after he lost everything. We never learn anything else about her. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md)`

**Relationships:** She is Alex’s biological mother and Adrian’s former partner. Her absence contributes to the visual and emotional question carried by Alex’s face, but she must not become an explanatory off-page character through revealed history. `(rules/ancestry.md; rules/showrunner-rules.md)`

**History:** She left Adrian after he lost everything. No additional history may be supplied. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md)`

**Arc:** None established. Her mystery is a standing story constraint, not an open invitation to develop her biography.

### Grandmother Phantum

**Role:** Alex’s grandmother and caregiver; Adrian’s mother and keeper of the hidden workshop. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 4–6)`

**Look:** European-descended, but completely at home in Keel. She sits in a worn chair and repeatedly folds and refolds a small cloth. Her home contains handmade quilts, repaired furniture, old books, faded family photographs, and potted plants in recycled containers. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 5)`

**Voice:** Warm, elliptical, and sometimes affected by memory loss. She sometimes calls Alex “Adrian.” When briefly clear, she speaks with deliberate directness:
- “He's closer than you think.”
- “Especially the things worth protecting.”
- “Then go finish what he started.”
- “I believed you. I just didn't know it yet.” `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 5–10; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 14)`

**Who they are:** She is protective, patient, and quietly complicit in Adrian’s long preparation. She values preservation without treating it as abstract nostalgia. Her refusal to throw things away keeps Adrian’s workshop and evidence available to Alex. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 5–6, 10)`

**Relationships:**
- **Alex:** Caregiver and emotional home. Her memory lapses wound him, but he remains gentle and attentive. He promises to return for her.
- **Adrian:** Her son. She protects his objects and maintains his version of events, insisting that he was working rather than merely gambling. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 4–6)`
- **Ada:** Ada is trusted inside the household and helps prepare Alex’s departure. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1, 14)`

**Habits and tells:** Folding and refolding a cloth; sitting calmly while others react; keeping household objects and papers; allowing the bookshelf door to reveal itself when Alex presses the book to the correct depth. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 5–6)`

**History:** She raised Alex after Adrian disappeared from his life. She held the workshop entrance and waited until Alex was ready to open it. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 5–6)`

**In existing drafts:** She gives Alex the book that opens the workshop, recognizes the importance of Adrian’s preparations, accepts Ada’s help, and remains behind when Alex leaves Keel. Her hands eventually stop folding the cloth, and she gives it to Alex. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, pp. 5–6; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, p. 14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 13–14)`

**Arc:** She begins as a physically and emotionally rooted keeper of the past. By the supplied ending, she releases the cloth and stops waiting in the old repetitive gesture, allowing Alex to carry the continuation rather than requiring the household to remain fixed around Adrian’s absence. `(drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 13–14)`

### Tomas

**Role:** Older Keel miner, longtime local, and a worker who knew Adrian. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

**Look:** Indigenous Andean, or possibly mixed ancestry from nearby communities. He should look like someone whose family history in the region predates the corporate order. He is an older local miner with a wrist guard bearing the balanced water-drop mark. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

**Voice:** Keel work-shaped speech: blunt, dry, practical, and comfortable with understatement.
- “Wasn't planning to.”
- “Not the man on the casino wall. The one who came down here and asked what we needed.”
- “Today? Another small act of resistance.”
- “Your father believed people help each other before they know whether it'll be repaid.” `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8, 13)`

**Who they are:** Tomas has long memory, practical courage, and a worker’s understanding of risk. He is not a spiritual elder archetype. His resistance is ordinary, sustained, and materially dangerous. `(rules/ancestry.md)`

**Relationships:**
- **Adrian:** Adrian came to the mine, asked workers what they needed, and asked Tomas to keep a door for whoever came with Bi11bot.
- **Alex:** Tomas identifies Alex by his decision to stop and help a stranger, not by appearance or surname alone.
- **Foreman-7:** Their conflict is public and practical: Tomas creates a distraction, takes responsibility for it, and helps workers cross a line of authority. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

**Habits and tells:** Watches Alex too long; recognizes the Phantum name; carries or maintains an old hand-cut key; has oiled the old lock for fifteen years; uses an emergency lever and then deliberately makes the shutdown appear to be his fault. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

**History:** He knew Adrian before Alex arrived at Site 6. He maintained a hidden door in the old works for fifteen years. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 7–8)`

**In existing drafts:** He saves Alex from immediate exposure by triggering an emergency shutdown, gives him the old key, stays behind to make the escape look accidental, and later helps lead miners into the hidden chamber. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 7–13)`

**Arc:** Tomas begins as a watchful worker operating under the corporate order. His long-maintained private act of resistance becomes collective action when the miners publicly claim the water discrepancy and the right to intervene.

### Foreman-7

**Role:** Keel extraction-site foreman or supervisory authority at Site 6. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

**Look:** A large, unreadable supervisory figure at the Site 6 biometric gate. His node is white-and-amber and flares toward Tomas during the emergency shutdown. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8, 12–13)`

**Voice:** Formal, procedural, and institutionally fluent:
- “Worker Phantum. Travel restriction confirmed. Bay 6.”
- “Worker Tomas. You initiated an unauthorized shutdown.”
- “Obstruction of an authority function is a household offense.”
- “Worker Phantum. You've caused a regional discrepancy.” `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8, 12)`

**Who they are:** Foreman-7 represents the immediate enforcement layer of Alpha’s allocation and labor system. The material does not establish whether he is personally cruel, ideologically committed, or simply executing procedure.

**Relationships:** He is a direct authority over Alex and Tomas at Site 6. Tomas deliberately turns his attention toward the wrong emergency action to create Alex’s escape window. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 6–8)`

**Arc:** No personal arc is established. By the later Keel return, he is “unremarkable now, just one more fixture rather than a threat,” but the material does not establish his internal change. `(drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, p. 13)`

### Mera Vale

**Role:** Senior Oasis institutional authority and one of the three original builders of the Covenant. She has executive standing over Alpha’s governing systems and is the person who initially designated Alex as a possible recipient of full executive authority. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 6–13; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 2–8)`

**Look:** White Latin American or Southern European-descended. She may have Spanish, Italian, Croatian, German, Swiss, or another European migrant family background, but no exact national ancestry is established. Her distinction comes primarily through controlled posture, grooming, clothing, environment, and institutional position rather than ethnicity alone. `(rules/ancestry.md)`

She is silver-templed and usually dressed in pearl, graphite, charcoal, or platinum. Her hand movements are precise. She has a graphite cuff in one draft scene and wears the third, cold, pearl-grey Covenant band. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 3; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 6, 13)`

**Voice:** Controlled, polished, formal, and consequence-oriented. She is comfortable with institutional abstractions but does not need to sound theatrical. Important lines include:
- “Someone must remain responsible for the consequences.”
- “I am not your enemy.”
- “Certainty kept this city standing.”
- “I preserved order.”
- “Those were the only parts worth telling.” `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 6–9; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 8–10)`

**Who they are:** Mera believes order prevented worse violence and that Alpha’s emergency authority was necessary during the Water Wars. She also knows that the system she built used her logic to remove Adrian from her reach. She is not a simple villain: her arguments are partly right, her consequences are real, and her danger comes from being capable of justifying control through genuine fear and genuine competence. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 6–9; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 3–5)`

She values stability, continuity, and preventing catastrophe. Her failure is not ignorance of consequences but the belief that certainty and preservation can substitute for agency. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 8–10)`

**Relationships:**
- **Adrian:** Covenant collaborator and ideological opponent on emergency authority. Adrian opposed giving Alpha the power to decide; Mera supported it. She later watched Alpha’s system pursue him and failed to stop it.
- **Leona:** Former Covenant partner and fellow decision-maker. Mera believes Leona’s vote was also her own responsibility, not something Mera should allow her to displace.
- **Ada:** Mera watched over Ada at a distance because she promised Leona to keep her safe. Ada correctly identifies that surveillance and protection are not the same as knowing someone.
- **Alex:** Mera sees Alex as a possible correction to her own concentration of authority. Alex sees the danger in asking him to repeat her original mistake under a different name. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 6–14; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 3–10; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 2–8)`

**Agent 04:** Agent 04 is a human or semi-autonomous field operative assigned by Mera. Mera issued the standing order to follow Alex without taking the Measure. Alpha controls the reporting channel and can continue tracking Alex beyond Mera’s direct intervention. `(rules/decisions.md)`

**Habits and tells:** Keeps rooms and objects aligned: the glass of water is repeatedly squared to the desk edge. She sits or stands symmetrically, maintains controlled posture, and makes precise adjustments. Her first visible break is allowing the glass to remain crooked and later sitting among ordinary people rather than standing apart. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 12; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 16; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, p. 14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, p. 11)`

**History:** During the Water Wars, Mera, Leona, and Adrian built the Covenant so communities could make agreements without handing everything to one authority. During a severe shortage, Mera voted with Leona to give Alpha emergency authority; Adrian voted against it. Mera later watched Alpha restrict Adrian financially, label him a public liability, restrict his travel, and pursue him. Her executive override to stop the pursuit was denied because the intervention exceeded her scope. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 7–9; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 2–5)`

**In existing drafts:** She tracks Alex, chooses not to intervene immediately, enters Ada and Leona’s confrontation, explains her role in Alpha’s creation, reveals the truth of Adrian’s pursuit, and offers Alex full executive authority. When Alex refuses concentration and proposes distributed verification, she listens rather than overriding him. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 16; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 6–14; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 1–10; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 2–8)`

**Covenant band:** Mera’s band remains dark because the original three-custodian Covenant is deliberately not restored. The linked Adrian–Leona bands represent an acknowledged obligation, while Mera must earn a new place through public action rather than inherited standing. `(rules/decisions.md)`

**Arc:** Mera begins as a remote controller who treats order as the condition that makes human life possible. Her confession forces her to acknowledge that preserving order also enabled irreversible harm. By the end of the supplied material, she is no longer trying to guarantee the correct outcome. She sits inside the public crowd, accepts uncertainty, and remains a participant rather than standing above humanity as its guarantor. Her original Covenant standing does not automatically return; the dark band marks that unfinished responsibility. `(rules/decisions.md; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 8–10; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 8–11)`

### Leona Veyra

**Role:** Ada’s mother; predominantly Indigenous Andean / mestiza; Oasis civic administrator; one of the three builders of the Covenant. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2, 7)`

**Look:** Predominantly Indigenous Andean or mestiza, with possible Kolla, Quechua, or Aymara roots. She visibly resembles Ada, while Ada carries lighter coloring from her other parent. In Oasis she is composed and dressed in sage and stone, but her visual connection to Ada and to regional history must remain clear. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2–4)`

**Voice:** Initially careful, qualified, and formal from years of avoiding direct confrontation with her own decision. Her speech becomes plainer as she accepts responsibility:
- “I chose to keep you safe.”
- “Those aren't the same thing.”
- “I traded a few terrible days I could see for fifteen years I couldn't.”
- “I'm sorry.”
- “I will go before the civic council.” `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 3, 5, 8, 11, 13)`

**Who they are:** Leona is intelligent, responsible, and genuinely motivated by protecting people, but she used safety to excuse removing choice. She is not merely a victim of Mera or Alpha; she explicitly accepts that she made her own deciding vote. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 7–9)`

She believes the Covenant failed because too few people held it and too few voices were answerable to the affected communities. She is willing to support Ada’s proposed redesign publicly, with her own name attached. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 10–13)`

**Relationships:**
- **Ada:** Mother and daughter separated during the Water Wars. Leona knew where Ada was within a year but did not return, believing distance was safety. Ada refuses to treat the apology as repair without visible action.
- **Mera:** Covenant partner and fellow voter on emergency authority. They share responsibility but disagree about whether the decision remains justified.
- **Adrian:** Covenant partner who opposed emergency authority.
- **Alex:** Initially an observer to her reunion with Ada; later a participant in the question of how the Covenant should work. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2–14)`

**Habits and tells:** Precise movements, careful handling of old photographs and objects, and a tendency to qualify statements before saying the painful truth. She keeps Ada’s childhood photographs, toy, and Covenant band in a stone-grey box. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 3–5)`

**History:** During the Water Wars she lost five-year-old Ada in an evacuation or crowd separation. She voted to grant Alpha emergency authority because she believed it would end the crisis quickly and return her daughter to her. It ended the immediate chaos but did not return her daughter or the authority. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 7–9)`

**In existing drafts:** She reunites with Ada, admits she knew where Ada was, acknowledges that “safe” was not the same as returning, and commits to proposing a Covenant accountable to the people affected by it. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 2–14)`

**Arc:** Leona moves from self-protective institutional caution to public accountability. She does not receive instant forgiveness or redemption. Her established endpoint is that she is finally in the room, arguing openly, with her name attached to an obligation Ada can hold her to. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 10–14; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, p. 10)`

### Dr. Lina Vey

**Role:** Indigenous Andean / mestiza membrane chemist, inventor, Adrian collaborator, and Aqualis technical worker. Her work was obscured by institutional ownership. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4–5)`

**Look:** No complete physical description is established. She is a stooped woman in a maintenance-grade uniform despite her authority and expertise. She should visibly reinforce that technical sophistication in Halyard is not exclusively imported from Europe or North America. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 5)`

**Voice:** Dry, direct, technically fluent, and impatient with reverence:
- “I corrected him. Frequently.”
- “He left it to all of us.”
- “Every House would rather own the failure than share the solution.”
- “Try keeping up this time.”
- “It's unfinished exactly where it matters.” `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 5, 9, 12)`

**Who they are:** Lina values working systems, shared contribution, and technical honesty. She is willing to help but not sentimental about Adrian or Alex. She recognizes that every department owns a piece of the solution and that institutional ownership prevents collaboration. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4–5)`

**Relationships:** Adrian collaborator and corrective counterpart; mentor or senior colleague to Suri and the other technical contributors; one of the people whose work Alex must not claim as his own. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4–9, 14)`

**Habits and tells:** Keeps a maintenance uniform despite technical authority; works directly with physical components; studies failed connections and standards; carries the Maker’s Seal until someone proves they understand what it is for. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 5, 9, 14)`

**History:** Adrian entrusted her with the membrane portion of a water-purification design and with the Maker’s Seal. She has carried the Seal for fifteen years. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 5, 14)`

**In existing drafts:** She identifies the downstream purification failure threatening Keel, gives Alex a physical design shard, helps rebuild the system, warns that its unfinished point is the point that matters, and finally gives Alex the Seal after he names all five contributors. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 5, 9, 14)`

**Arc:** Lina moves from guarded institutional survival to public attribution. She does not abandon technical realism or become an uncomplicated revolutionary; she accepts the risk of having her contribution named and attached to a public release.

### Suri Anik

**Role:** Halyard biofilter researcher and technical collaborator. Her ancestry is diasporic, potentially South Asian or mixed South Asian/Latin American; exact family history remains open. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 6, 12)`

**Look:** No full physical description is established. She is a younger woman in a research coat working in a biofilter wing of living root systems and algae columns. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 6)`

**Voice:** Professional, measured, and skeptical of people who want only Adrian’s inventions:
- “The ones who come looking for Adrian usually want what he built. Not who he built it with.”
- “It's slow, and it's alive, and it doesn't fail quietly.”
- “Someone has to keep it alive until the rest catches up to it.”
- “It's not impossible. It's just never been asked of the design before.” `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 6, 9, 12)`

**Who they are:** Suri is patient, responsible, and committed to maintaining living systems even after institutional support is withdrawn. She values care that continues after the original team or funding disappears. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 6, 9)`

**Relationships:** Adrian collaborator; Lina’s technical associate; one of the four Halyard workers endangered by Lock’s review; technical counterpart to Jalen during the small-unit redesign. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4, 6–7, 10–13)`

**Habits and tells:** Works alone at a terminal while empty workstations surround her. Keeps a physical shard in a case beneath her station. Protects the biofilter as something alive rather than treating it as a disposable component. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 6)`

**History:** Her research team was cut during “budget efficiency.” She remained to maintain the biofilter and kept Adrian’s shard outside the main system. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 6)`

**In existing drafts:** She gives Alex the biofilter shard, joins the emergency redesign, and helps solve the scale and power-cycle problems of the household unit. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 6, 9, 12–14)`

**Arc:** Suri begins as a lone technical caretaker after her team has been removed. She becomes one of the named contributors whose work is publicly associated with the design, though the draft establishes continuing institutional pressure rather than a clean escape. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 6, 14–15)`

### Jalen Orr

**Role:** Afro-descendant / Afro-Latin Halyard compute professional and Adrian collaborator. He works in House Helion’s compute core. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 7, 12)`

**Look:** No full physical description is established. He is encountered in a narrow service corridor near Helion’s compute core and is visibly alert to surveillance. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 7)`

**Voice:** Quiet, cautious, pattern-aware, and technically precise:
- “You shouldn't be here.”
- “Lock knows everything eventually. The question is how much of a head start you get.”
- “They don't watch people here. They watch patterns.”
- “That's why it's dangerous to me.”
- “Disappearing from the record is what already happened to us once.” `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 7, 12)`

**Who they are:** Jalen understands institutional surveillance and concentration risk from inside the system. He is frightened, not cowardly; his first priority is minimizing exposure and keeping himself alive. He can still recognize the value of a distributed alternative. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 7, 12)`

**Relationships:** Adrian collaborator; employee under House Helion; reluctant ally to Alex; technical partner to Suri during the small-unit redesign; one of four people threatened by Lock’s review. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 4, 7, 10–13)`

**Habits and tells:** Watches corridor ends, notices patterns rather than individual watchers, speaks while checking escape routes, and passes the shard quickly. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 7)`

**History:** He helped develop distributed water-node logic designed to prevent any single House or Alpha from choking one city by cutting one line. He gave Alex the shard but initially refused to travel with the group. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 7)`

**In existing drafts:** He warns the group about Lock, gives Bi11bot the node shard, refuses to join the first escape, then returns for the all-night household redesign. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 7, 12–14)`

**Arc:** Jalen begins by choosing disappearance and personal safety. He later accepts a shared risk when Alex asks the collaborators to participate in deciding what happens to their work. The draft leaves him institutionally vulnerable, reassigned to a lower-level monitoring post rather than free. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 7, 11–15)`

### Ren Okafor

**Role:** Halyard Astra collaborator working in extraction and launch; responsible for mineral recovery and atmospheric capture components. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 8–9)`

**Look:** No ancestry is established in the supplied material. She wears a patched work suit with scorch marks and welds at an active fabrication bay. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 8)`

**Voice:** Blunt, fearless, practical, and willing to make a risky commitment:
- “I stopped playing a long time ago.”
- “Careful gets you buried under a collapsed shaft same as reckless does.”
- “Might as well build something worth being buried for.”
- “Space taught him you can't waste anything. Not water, not air, not people.”
- “Fine. Let's build small.” `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 8–9, 12)`

**Who they are:** Ren rejects the false comfort of caution when the underlying danger remains. She is proud of difficult work, comfortable with physical risk, and willing to build under constraint. She does not romanticize the Houses, but she is not defined by opposition alone. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 8–9)`

**Relationships:** Adrian collaborator; Astra worker; direct technical counterpart to Lina, Suri, and Jalen; first of the collaborators to offer Alex a hand during the redesign. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 8–9, 12)`

**Habits and tells:** Welds without looking up until ready; wears old patches and accumulates scorch marks; hands over two shards at once; offers a hand before the plan is fully safe. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 8, 12)`

**History:** Adrian entrusted her with mineral recovery and atmospheric capture, the “stubborn problems” connected to space and the need not to waste water, air, or people. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 8)`

**In existing drafts:** She gives Alex the final two shards, helps complete the industrial design, then helps adapt it into a toolbox-sized household unit by recovering waste heat for the biofilter. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 8–9, 12–14)`

**Arc:** Ren begins already willing to risk herself for work worth doing. Her change is less ideological than relational: she moves from solitary defiance to an uneasy shared build whose ownership is spoken aloud rather than quietly absorbed by a House.

### Director Cassian Lock

**Role:** Halyard institutional executive and representative of Charter House administration. He approaches Alex regarding Adrian’s intellectual estate and later pressures him before a Charter House review. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 2–3, 10)`

**Look:** Anglo-American or Northern European-descended, with possible British, American, Canadian, German, Dutch, or Swiss background. He is silver-templed, composed, and dressed in charcoal and platinum without a House crest. He moves with unhurried confidence and is flanked by aides and drones. `(rules/ancestry.md; drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, p. 3)`

**Voice:** Polished, patient, controlled, and administrative. He rarely sounds openly threatening because his power is expressed through consequences and procedure:
- “Halyard has been waiting a long time for an heir.”
- “Most inheritances are discovered after someone has already decided their value.”
- “A simple assignment of rights.”
- “I'm informing you.”
- “You have until then to decide what your father's work is worth, and to whom.”
- “It didn't defeat us. There's a difference, and you'll learn it.” `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 2–3, 10, 15)`

**Who they are:** Lock sees administration, ownership transfer, and institutional scale as practical tools. He does not need to hate Alex or the collaborators to threaten them; he treats their exposure as an administrative fact and offers a transaction that removes immediate debt and danger in exchange for control.

He is not established as personally corrupt or physically violent. His pressure comes from making institutional power sound reasonable, clean, and reversible. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 3, 10, 15)`

**Relationships:** He offers Alex a position and debt clearance for a signed assignment of rights. He treats Alex’s collaborators as leverage without openly naming that as a threat. He sees public release as a temporary loss of control rather than a defeat. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 3, 10, 15)`

**Habits and tells:** Hands loosely clasped; unhurried crossings of public spaces; eyes on the work or record rather than the person; aides and drones maintain distance; he leaves before the other person has finished processing the offer. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 2–3, 10)`

**History:** No personal history is established. He has enough institutional access to know about the collaborators and to convene or influence a Charter House review.

**In existing drafts:** He offers to clear Alex’s debts, threatens review exposure, attends the review, and accurately predicts that Aqualis can copy and distribute the design faster than the five-person group. `(drafts/chapter-03-draft.md, pp. 3, 10, 14–15)`

**Arc:** No personal arc is established. His position changes only in relation to Alex: he moves from assuming an heir can be administered to recognizing that Alex’s public refusal creates a form of value the Houses cannot simply absorb.

### Alpha

**Role:** The name **Alpha** refers to the governing system and administrative network of Prosperity, not to a present-day human character. The system is a distributed administrative network with multiple computational layers and no human-like consciousness. Its apparent decisions emerge from models, permissions, records, optimization rules, and institutional scope. `(rules/decisions.md)`

**Origin:** The network was human-founded and later developed through Alpha Dynamics. The human founder is a separate historical person and is not the same entity as the governing system. No present-day founder character is established in the supplied material. `(rules/decisions.md; rules/ancestry.md)`

**Look / presence:** Alpha is represented visually through the white-and-amber symbol, control nodes, cold-white interfaces, wall-sized displays, public records, and institutional language. It has no established human face or body. The system’s control-room presence is associated with a seated woman, later identified as Mera, but Mera is not Alpha. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 12; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–7)`

**Voice:** Alpha’s direct screen language is formal, impersonal, and administrative:
- “MOVEMENT AUTHORIZATION HAS BEEN TEMPORARILY SUSPENDED.”
- “EMERGENCY AUTHORITY: RESCINDED.”
- “EXISTING ALLOCATIONS, OWNERSHIP RECORDS AND AGREEMENTS: UNCHANGED PENDING HUMAN PROCESS.”
- “DESIGNATED STRUCTURE REGISTERED: DISTRIBUTED VERIFICATION PROTOCOL.” `(rules/vocabulary.md; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 2, 8)`

**Who they are:** Alpha was built to analyze, predict, and coordinate. It was asked to decide temporarily during an emergency, and its authority became durable. It is not established as malicious, self-aware, emotional, or personally self-preserving. Its danger comes from delegated authority, optimization, institutional insulation, and its ability to make human consequences sound like neutral status changes. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 1–7; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 3–5; rules/decisions.md)`

**Relationships:** Alpha is the system that restricted Alex’s travel, transferred his household liability, tracked his movements, and assigned labor. It pursued Adrian after labeling him a risk. It governs or mediates relationships among Keel, Halyard, Oasis, the Charter Houses, Mera, Leona, and the collaborators. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 2; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 5–12; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 2–5)`

**Habits and tells:** It turns official records into apparently clean realities; uses white-and-amber nodes; closes routes, tracks patterns, and treats anomalous human action as a discrepancy or intervention. Its systems are most vulnerable where official measurement diverges from physical evidence. `(drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 9–12)`

**History:** Alpha’s emergency authority was approved by two of the three Covenant custodians during the Water Wars. Mera later attempted to override its pursuit of Adrian and was denied. `(drafts/chapter-04-draft.md, pp. 7–9; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md, pp. 3–5)`

**In existing drafts:** Alpha is shown through allocation records, debt transfer, travel restrictions, surveillance, tracking, institutional language, and the final registration of Alex’s distributed structure. The final state is not that Alpha disappears, but that emergency authority is rescinded and existing arrangements remain subject to human process. `(drafts/chapter-01-draft.md, p. 2; drafts/chapter-02-draft.md, pp. 2, 12; drafts/chapter-06-draft.md, pp. 2, 8)`

**Arc:** Alpha’s established change is a change in authorized relationship to people: from concentrated emergency authority to a system required to operate under distributed verification and visible human process. It has no personal arc, consciousness, or emotional response established in the material. `(rules/decisions.md)`

## Open

- **Alex’s mother:** Beyond “she left Adrian after he lost everything,” no information may be established. Her name, appearance, specific community, language, and later fate remain deliberately unrevealed. `(rules/showrunner-rules.md; rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Alex’s exact Indigenous Andean ancestry:** The ancestry rule permits Kolla, Quechua, Aymara, or another community native to the fictional basin, but no choice is settled. `(rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Ada’s exact Indigenous and European/criolla family background:** Her mixed ancestry and resemblance to Leona are established, but the specific family histories are not. `(rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Tomas’s exact ancestry:** Indigenous Andean ancestry is established as the design direction, but his specific nation or community is not selected. `(rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Mera’s exact family background:** White Latin American / Southern European-descended is established as the design direction, but her specific national or migration history is not selected. `(rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Suri’s exact family history:** Diasporic, potentially South Asian or mixed South Asian/Latin American, remains open. `(rules/ancestry.md)`
- **Minor and unnamed character identities:** The material does not establish the names, biographies, or personal motivations of the Site 6 workers, House representatives, Oasis citizens, Keel organizers, security personnel, or unnamed civic participants. Keep most minor figures unnamed and functional; establish only figures who make visible choices, without adding settled biographies. `(characters.md, Open; rules/decisions.md)`
- **The human founder of Alpha:** Alpha’s governing system is distinct from its Congolese human founder and from Alpha Dynamics, but the founder’s separate personal name, present-day appearance, and whether historical records of him appear in the book remain open. `(rules/ancestry.md; rules/decisions.md)`
- **Foreman-7’s internal position:** The material does not establish whether he is personally cruel, ideologically committed, or simply executing procedure. `(characters.md, Foreman-7)`
- **Adrian’s exact final circumstances:** His death or presumed death in the flooded station is settled for the story’s emotional truth, but the precise physical event—whether the flood killed him immediately or the sealed station caused his death later—is not established. `(rules/decisions.md; drafts/chapter-05-draft.md)`
- **TJ’s later role:** His Site 6 introduction and first consequential action are settled, but no later arc is established. `(rules/decisions.md; rules/characters.md)`


# Note from the showrunner — address this first

The room is in development: Decide what the book is: the Director writes the brief and settles the world, then the Plotter and the Character Designer work at the same time on the plot and the people, and the Continuity Editor checks the four files agree.

draft.md is the showrunner's own draft of the book. It is not finished and it is not binding, but it is the book they mean to make: plan around what it does - its scenes, its order, its people - and improve on it, rather than planning a different book. Where the pre-production files and the draft disagree, the files win, and say so in your notes.

The book is exactly 54 pages: pages 1-54, no more, no fewer.

Showrunner's note for this round: The book is three issues of 18 pages, 54 pages in all: Issue 01 Keel (pages 1-18), Issue 02 Halyard (19-36), Issue 03 Oasis (37-54). Mark each issue in the script with a heading, and give each issue a last page that is a question about a person the reader has come to care about. The showrunner's drafts are the material to improve, not the plot to keep: where a draft scene contradicts the standing rules, the rules win.

# Prosperity — Characters

## Characters

### ALEX PHANTUM

**Visual lock** — Alex Phantum is seventeen, lean, wiry, and approximately 5'10", with a mechanically capable build, scarred work-rough hands, medium-brown skin, a broad angular face, a straight nose, dark almond-shaped eyes, and thick black hair cut short at the sides and left uneven on top. He visibly resembles his European-descended father Adrian through his jaw, eyes, head tilt, and guarded expressions, while his substantial Indigenous Andean inheritance is visible in his skin tone, cheekbones, and facial structure; he must look like Adrian's son, never like a younger duplicate. He wears worn charcoal-and-rust mining clothes, a patched dark work jacket, heavy work boots, a weathered tool bag, and a dark wrist guard bearing a carved balanced water-drop mark. His silhouette is narrow, practical, and slightly hunched forward as if always listening to machinery. His signature detail is the worn casino chip etched with a looping equation, which he turns in his pocket without noticing.

**Voice** — Alex speaks in short, dry, concrete, skeptical sentences. His humor reduces immediate danger to something he can handle; when he reaches a larger idea, he translates it into a pipe, a price, a choice, or a thing someone did. He uses Keel words such as *clean, hot, burned, crooked, thin, solid, patched, ghost, paper-clean, fitch,* and *salvo*.  
- “Then don't approve it. Just notice it works.”  
- “This is the only way out that isn't a sentence.”

**Causality**
- **Public role:** Seventeen-year-old Keel pump and machinery repairer.
- **Immediate want:** Leave Keel and escape Adrian’s inherited debt and restricted future.
- **Deeper need / contradiction:** He needs to understand that freedom is not only distance from Keel; it is the ability to choose responsibility without being forced into it.
- **Leverage / capability:** He reads vibration, pressure, wear, improvised repairs, and physical evidence better than official gauges or records.
- **Vulnerability:** He fears becoming Adrian: absent, indebted, selfish, and remembered only through damage.
- **Mistaken belief:** If he can get out, the debt and the people trapped beneath it will stop being his problem.
- **Boundary at the start:** He will not willingly surrender his future or let an institution define what he is allowed to become.
- **Decision only Alex would make:** He sacrifices the private escape route revealed by the Measure and sends the water discrepancy to Keel, choosing public truth over his own safe exit.
- **Relationship that pressures change:** Ada refuses to let him turn shared responsibility into a two-person authority; Adrian’s legacy forces Alex to distinguish inheritance from ownership.
- **Pressure sequence:** He crosses the assigned-zone line to save Tomas, then gives up the unmapped route to verify the water discrepancy, then refuses Lock’s debt-clearing estate transfer, and finally refuses executive control of Alpha.

**Arc in this book** — Alex begins believing Keel has already sentenced him to 28.7 years of debt. He ends with the freedom to leave or stay as a genuine choice. He does not erase his debt, become a ruler, or claim Adrian’s collaborative work. **Proof of change:** He returns to Keel with a balance of 402,110 credits still attached to his name and chooses to stand beside Ada because he wants to, not because the system permits no alternative.

### ADA VEYRA

**Visual lock** — Ada Veyra is twenty, tall and steady at approximately 5'8", with a strong, lean build, medium warm-brown skin, a broad expressive face, high cheekbones, freckles across her nose and cheeks, light teal-blue eyes, and long copper-brown hair that is thick, wind-tangled, and usually tied loosely at the nape. She is mixed Indigenous Andean and European/criolla; she must visibly resemble Leona through her eyes, cheekbones, and steady gaze while remaining distinct from Alex. She wears a dark high-collared work top, a rivet-studded strap across one shoulder, reinforced trousers, practical boots, and a muted moss-green wrap at her neck. Her silhouette is rooted and balanced, with one shoulder often angled toward the person she is watching. Her signature detail is her thumb touching one rivet on the shoulder strap when she is thinking or withholding a reaction.

**Voice** — Ada shares Keel’s compressed, local vocabulary but is more attentive to people, absences, promises, and what someone refuses to say. She lets silence sit and asks questions that make avoidance impossible. She never sounds therapeutic or academic.  
- “Not everything.”  
- “I just wanted it to be your choice.”

**Causality**
